articles.title: Why has Brittany Mahomes stopped posing warmly with Patrick Mahomes’ younger brother Jackson Mahomes
articles.summary: Brittany Mahomes used to be a frequent visitor on her brother-in-law Jackson Mahomes’ Instagram account.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes used to be a frequent visitor on her brother-in-law Jackson Mahomes’ Instagram account.However, since the 2026 NFL season began, Patrick Mahomes’ brother hasn’t posted any photos with the mother of three. Even his most recent IG post features one of Brittany’s children rather than Brittany herself.While Brittany appeared in nearly every other photo from June 2019 until September 2025, she has rarely been featured since. Currently, only a few pictures on his Instagram include her, and in those, she appears alongside the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback, his mother Randi Mahomes, and his half-sister Mia Randall.Brittany Mahomes and Jackson Mahomes’ changing relationshipBrittany Mahomes went from wearing the brightest smile while posing with Jackson Mahomes to sporting a subtle, “not-interested-in-posing-with-you” look over the course of six years.On the other hand, Jackson’s smile never changed in the slightest; he looks just as radiant as he did in their very first photo together. However, Brittany’s shifting attitude toward her brother-in-law is now impossible to miss.He was there helping her choose her wedding dress, celebrating her birthdays, and helping take care of her kids. But now? Suddenly, everything has changed.Fans were so used to seeing them together that when Jackson appeared to hard-launch his relationship with Shyanne Blankenship on Instagram, one user commented, “Ain’t that Brittany Mahomes?”Another wrote, “Looks like big bro’s wife,” while a third added, “Resemble Brittany.” A fourth user simply asked, “Why does that look like Brittany?” That is just how frequently the two used to post together.Maybe his Kansas City influencer girlfriend dislikes him posing with his brother’s wife on Instagram, though that is pure speculation. Ultimately, anything could explain the drop in posts.Alternatively, maybe Brittany disapproves of Jackson dating Shyanne Blankenship, leading her to stop posing with him with her signature bright smile.Jackson’s 2021 birthday post for Brittany read, “HBD to my bestie/sidekick and future sister. Loved celebrating you.” If Brittany was once that close to him, maybe she dislikes his current girlfriend - or maybe she is simply too busy managing three children and several multimillion-dollar business ventures.Or did that viral 2024 Super Bowl party video have something to do with a potential fallout? Jackson appeared to be denied entry into a VIP section during a Future concert in Las Vegas, right where his sister-in-law was standing.When the security guard blocked Jackson, he looked in Brittany’s direction, seemingly hoping she would intervene. Instead, she shrugged and kept dancing.Or did Kayla Nicole have something to do with the fallout between the two?Brittany Mahomes’ constant presence on Jackson Mahomes’ InstagramEvery year, the wife of the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback has appeared alongside members of the Mahomes family at football games and several of their celebrations.Jackson has shared updates and personal moments from those celebrations with his Instagram followers, maintaining a strong social media presence over the past six years.He has also posed with Kayla Nicole, Travis Kelce’s ex-girlfriend and Brittany’s former close friend. Their previous public appearances have included family celebrations and football-related events.In May 2025, Jackson reposted Brittany’s Instagram story, in which the NFL WAG posed in a risque, one-shouldered dress and sat alongside her friend Miranda and Jackson. She captioned it, “Happy Birthdayyyy!!!!! [Jackson Mahomes].”Jackson Mahomes’ Instagram posts spark rift speculationBeing part of a high-profile NFL family means even slight changes in social media activity attract widespread public scrutiny.Patrick Mahomes’ career with the Kansas City Chiefs has kept the Mahomes family in the spotlight for nearly a decade. On the other hand, Brittany Mahomes has created her own public profile through business ventures, fitness, and lifestyle content on her social media account.Consequently, a smaller number of joint photos cannot reliably measure family closeness or indicate a rift. There may be nothing wrong at all; relatives often remain close without regularly appearing together online.However, Brittany’s lack of expected presence in Jackson Mahomes’ Instagram posts does spark rift speculation.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: In January 2026, Operation Breakthrough students gave Travis Kelce heartfelt praise for his down-to-earth nature and continued involvement in their lives.
articles.body: In January 2026, Operation Breakthrough students gave Travis Kelce heartfelt praise for his down-to-earth nature and continued involvement in their lives. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end made an everlasting impression on these students through his humble interactions.He offered encouraging words, memorable experiences, and opportunities beyond football. These students highlighted how the 11-time Pro Bowler’s willingness to listen patiently and join in their day-to-day activities helped them feel deeply valued and loved.One student summed up Kelce’s personality, saying, “This sort of groundedness you wouldn’t expect to see in a lot of NFL players.” Because Kelce wasn’t talking about his football stats; he was trying to understand how the student’s school day went.Travis Kelce’s Operation Breakthrough involvementOne student said Travis Kelce had been involved with Operation Breakthrough for as long as they could remember. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end participated in robotics competitions and casual pizza celebrations after robotics practice.Another student recalled how Kelce gave them a Super Bowl ticket in 2025. That experience became a memorable moment. It changed their perspective and gave them a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to travel to another state. They experienced the new culture and witnessed the much-celebrated event in person.Some of the students recalled personal encounters with the NFL megastar. One met Travis Kelce at a mall. They filmed a video with him at Champs. Also invited him to eat pizza for dinner. Kelce, without a flinch, wholeheartedly accepted the invitation.Travis Kelce supports young studentsThe three-time Super Bowl champion’s interest in children extends beyond participation in Operation Breakthrough activities.One student remembered being unexpectedly approached by Travis Kelce. Kelce enquired about his grades. The question made the student nervous at first, but it also showed Kelce’s interest in children’s academic progress. The student felt special because an important person wanted to know their grades.One student recalled how Kelce shared his personal experience with them. The NFL superstar helped them understand how to handle adversity both on the field and in everyday life.Sharing his experience of being under constant public scrutiny, he explained how he manages that pressure while staying as authentic as possible. One student spoke very highly of Kelce.The student credited him for encouraging a positive attitude towards life. The student’s experience speaks volumes about how exposure to different career fields can help youth understand their individual interests, develop skills, and explore future career paths.Travis Kelce’s humility wins students’ praiseOne student was highly impressed by Travis Kelce’s humility. articles.title: "We are grateful for Tom’s generous support”: How Tom Brady donated his $170,000 Salem State speaking fee to Best Buddies and other charities to help those in need
articles.summary: Tom Brady earned $170,000 for a one-hour speaking appearance at Salem State University in May 2015.
articles.body: Tom Brady earned $170,000 for a one-hour speaking appearance at Salem State University in May 2015. But the former New England Patriots quarterback reportedly gave away the entire fee, sending $50,000 to Best Buddies and the rest to other charities. The donation came during a difficult stretch in his NFL career, with the Deflategate controversy dominating headlines and a four-game suspension hanging over him.The event attracted around 4,000 people, but Brady’s decision to donate the money gave the appearance another dimension. Here is how the payment, the charity contribution and his existing relationship with Best Buddies came together. Tom Brady gave away his $170,000 Salem State speaking feeSalem State University confirmed on June 16, 2015, that its nonprofit foundation had paid Brady $170,000 for his appearance at the school’s annual speaker series on May 7. Also, Boston Globe reported that Brady had donated the fee to charity, citing information from Best Buddies.According to the report, Best Buddies received $50,000, while other charities shared the remaining $120,000. The organization did not identify the other recipients in its announcement.Anthony Kennedy Shriver, Best Buddies’ founder and chairman, confirmed the contribution in a statement to The Boston Globe. “We are grateful for Tom’s generous support over the years,” Shriver said.The payment also raised questions about the cost of bringing a celebrity speaker to a public university. Salem State said ticket sales and corporate sponsorships covered Brady’s fee. The foundation made a profit of about $40,000 from the event, according to the university.Around 4,000 people attended the appearance. Tickets ranged from $20 to $100, with students paying $15, according to an Associated Press report published by CBS Boston on June 17, 2015.Brady also faced questions about Deflategate during the event. Speaking with television reporter Jim Gray at Salem State on May 7, he addressed the NFL investigation but declined to offer a detailed response to its findings.“I don’t really have any reaction [to the Wells Report]. It has only been 30 hours. I’ve not had much time to digest it,” Brady said during the Salem State appearance.His donation came as the NFL prepared to enforce a four-game suspension over the controversy. Brady appealed the punishment, setting up a dispute with commissioner Roger Goodell. Best Buddies already had a strong relationship with Tom BradyThe $50,000 contribution continued Brady’s support for Best Buddies, a nonprofit that promotes friendships and opportunities for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.Brady had helped the organization raise money through an annual charity football game at Harvard Stadium. The event brought together celebrities and children to support its work.The 2015 game took place at the end of May, just weeks after his Salem State appearance. Some fans wore “Free Brady” shirts at the fundraiser while the quarterback challenged his suspension.That existing relationship helps explain why Best Buddies featured prominently in the donation announcement. However, the organization’s statement did not say how Brady divided the remaining $120,000 among other charities.The Salem State appearance also had a financial benefit for the university. The foundation used ticket sales and corporate sponsorships to cover the speaking fee and other event expenses, and the school reported a profit rather than a loss.Brady’s donation therefore involved more than one charitable contribution. He gave Best Buddies $50,000, directed the rest of his speaking fee to other charities and continued supporting an organization with which he had an established fundraising relationship. The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback's long-awaited reunion with his family was supposed to mark a fresh start. However, a new report is raising questions about just how close everyone really is, especially when it comes to his younger brother, Jordan Rodgers, and his mystery wife, Brittani.Aaron Rodgers’ family reunion not so picture-perfect? Brother Jordan reportedly knows little about mystery wifeAccording to a new report, an insider claims that Jordan and his wife, JoJo Fletcher, don't seem to know much about Brittani. The source also hinted that the relationship between the brothers might not be completely back on track, despite their recent efforts to reconnect.And honestly, that detail makes this family reunion story even more interesting. Aaron has credited Brittani with helping him open the door to reconciliation, yet his brother's reported lack of familiarity with her suggests that the family's journey toward healing could be more complicated than it looks.Aaron's relationship with his family has been a topic of conversation for years. The quarterback's estrangement from his parents and siblings became public knowledge during Jordan's appearance on The Bachelorette in 2016, when Jordan spoke about their distant relationship.For a long time, there were few signs of a meaningful reconciliation. That began to change this year, when Aaron shared glimpses of spending time with his parents and older brother, Luke.The quarterback later opened up about reconnecting with Jordan, too. During an appearance on Cam Heyward's Not Just Football podcast in September, Aaron confirmed that the brothers had met and described their conversation as a tough one.Brittani is perhaps the most intriguing person in this story because Aaron has kept his marriage largely out of the public eye. Aaron confirmed that he was married in June 2025, but has deliberately kept details about his wife private. Unlike many celebrity couples, the two have largely avoided sharing their relationship with the world.Aaron has credited Brittani with helping him become more open to repairing his family relationships. Her encouragement reportedly played a role in his decision to reconnect with his parents and siblings after years of estrangement.That's what makes the insider's claim about Jordan and JoJo particularly interesting. If the report is accurate, Aaron's wife has been an important figure in his reconciliation journey, while his younger brother's household apparently remains unfamiliar with her.Earlier reporting also indicated that Jordan and JoJo did not attend Aaron's wedding. However, neither that absence nor the latest insider comments independently prove that Brittani is the reason behind any lingering tension.Jordan Rodgers has shown public support for his brotherDespite their complicated history, Jordan hasn't appeared entirely disconnected from Aaron.Jordan publicly defended his brother's football performance during an appearance on ESPN's First Take in September, praising Aaron's play and discussing the expectations surrounding the Steelers.Jordan also liked a family post shared by their older brother Luke after a Steelers gathering, even though he wasn't pictured with the group. Those gestures don't reveal what is happening behind closed doors, but they do offer a more nuanced picture than a simple story of two brothers falling out all over again.Jordan and JoJo also have their own lives and commitments, making it difficult to draw conclusions from their absence at a family gathering. articles.title: 49ers’ perfect DeForest Buckner trade offer to Colts before NFL trade deadline
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers should offer the Indianapolis Colts a 2027 third-round pick for DeForest Buckner before the November 10 NFL trade deadline. That is a...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers should offer the Indianapolis Colts a 2027 third-round pick for DeForest Buckner before the November 10 NFL trade deadline. That is a meaningful price for a 32-year-old defensive tackle, but his production and fit make a reunion worth pursuing.

This would not be about correcting an unpopular decision from six years ago. It would be about acquiring an interior difference-maker for a championship push while giving Indianapolis a valuable asset for its next roster overhaul.

Why Buckner would elevate San Francisco's defensive front

Buckner has recorded 26 tackles, four sacks and three passes defended through six games in 2026. He also has eight quarterback hits and four tackles for loss. Those numbers show a veteran still influencing possessions rather than surviving on reputation.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

That interior disruption is what San Francisco should prioritize. Edge pressure becomes more dangerous when quarterbacks cannot comfortably step forward, and Buckner can challenge guards while creating less predictable escape routes.

His arrival would also broaden the defensive coordinator's options. The 49ers could pursue pressure with four rushers more confidently, preserving additional defenders in coverage instead of depending on extra blitzers to manufacture disruption.

There is a run-defense benefit, too. Buckner's ability to penetrate can force runners to alter their paths before reaching the second level. That creates opportunities for teammates, provided the entire front maintains its gap responsibilities.

Familiarity adds appeal without eliminating the adjustment period. Buckner spent his first four NFL seasons with San Francisco, and Kyle Juszczyk has publicly encouraged him to return. Existing relationships could help his integration, although the current scheme and personnel still require study.

The contract creates urgency and risk. Buckner is in the final year of his deal, so San Francisco would be acquiring immediate help without guaranteed control beyond this season. An extension could be discussed separately, but the trade should make sense even without one.

Why Indianapolis should consider moving its defensive leader

The Colts are 2-4, making their deadline decision more complicated than simply declaring themselves contenders or sellers. Trading Buckner would weaken the defense immediately and remove an established locker-room presence.

Still, Indianapolis must weigh that loss against the possibility of watching him leave in free agency. A guaranteed third-round selection would provide a concrete return now rather than relying on an uncertain future compensatory-pick outcome.

That selection could help address several needs. The Colts could draft a replacement defender, strengthen another position or use it as part of a larger transaction. Younger contributors on rookie contracts would give the organization greater flexibility around its next core.

Financial considerations matter, but neither team should confuse Buckner's full 2026 cap charge with the amount transferred in a deadline trade. Previously paid bonus accounting and remaining compensation require separate analysis before any agreement.

The perfect offer balances impact against rental risk

The proposed package should remain straightforward:

San Francisco's 2027 third-round draft pick.

For Indianapolis, a third-rounder acknowledges that Buckner remains a premium contributor rather than a veteran being discarded. For San Francisco, it preserves first- and second-round selections while addressing an immediate need with a proven player.

The 49ers should resist adding another substantial asset unless competing bids justify it. Buckner's age and expiring contract impose a sensible ceiling, even with his strong performance.

This is the kind of calculated aggression contenders should embrace: pay for present impact, respect the long-term cost and avoid letting familiarity replace disciplined evaluation.

Jason Kelce had a memorable moment with Kansas City Chiefs fans ahead of the team's Oct. 18, 2026, game against the Los Angeles Chargers. During a pregame tailgate outside Arrowhead Stadium, the retired NFL center watched a fan sink an unusually long basketball shot and immediately connected the moment to WNBA star Caitlin Clark.

articles.title: Steelers’ Paris bar fan event’s fate sealed amid protests
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers will no longer hold their planned Steelers House gathering in Paris this weekend after recent protests prompted security concerns aro...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers will no longer hold their planned Steelers House gathering in Paris this weekend after recent protests prompted security concerns around the event's location.

Pittsburgh canceled the fan gathering at a bar in the Bastille neighborhood ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the New Orleans Saints . The decision affects the team-sponsored event but does not change plans for Sunday's game at Stade de France.

"Following recent events in the Bastille neighborhood, and after careful consideration, we felt it appropriate not to move forward with the planned Steelers House fan event in Paris," a message sent to fans read, according to The Associated Press.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Steelers described the decision as a precaution after the Bastille area experienced recent disruptions. Additional demonstrations could also take place in Paris and other areas of France over the weekend.

The NFL's broader activities in the city have continued without interruption. Nicki Ewell, the league's vice president for global events, told the AP that Pittsburgh made the call to cancel Steelers House. The NFL helped distribute the announcement after previously working with the team to promote the gathering.

Ewell said other NFL fan events have not been affected.

An Irish pub called O'Sullivans in the Bastille area had also advertised a watch party for Sunday's Steelers-Saints matchup.

Roger Goodell addresses security ahead of Steelers' Paris clash

The Steelers reiterated that the league continues to coordinate with local officials as preparations for the game continue.

"The NFL, as they do for every game, including international games, is working closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters," the Steelers said in a statement to the AP. "As stated by the NFL, there have been no disruptions or impacts at League sites."

NFL commissioner Roger Goodell addressed the unrest Wednesday and expressed confidence that the league has taken the necessary precautions for its Paris game.

Goodell said he spoke with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, while officials have remained in communication with authorities in Paris and throughout France.

"We've made all the preparations," Goodell said. "Protests are not unusual in France, as you know, and that's something that we will be aware of and make sure that the appropriate arrangements are made."

The cancellation therefore remains limited to Pittsburgh's designated Bastille bar event rather than Sunday's game.

The Steelers enter Week 7 at 4-2, while the Saints sit at 2-4. Pittsburgh and New Orleans will meet Sunday at Stade de France, with kickoff scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network.

articles.title: Ravens' Marlon Humphrey Calls Out Lamar Jackson 'Slander,' Says QB Gets 'Unfair Treatment'
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey defended teammate and quarterback Lamar Jackson on Thursday in a chat with reporters.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey defended teammate and quarterback Lamar Jackson on Thursday in a chat with reporters.

"It seems like Lamar's the only quarterback kind of gets the slander that he gets for anytime anything is going on," Humphrey said, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley . "I feel like you just don't see these same articles. I'm in the hot tub and it's this, that and the third. Unfair treatment."

Per Hensley, Humphrey was asked if he was referencing injury "slander." Hensley said Humphrey didn't specify, but the four-time Pro Bowler added the following remarks:

"I just feel like sometimes it seems like it gets away from ... I don't know if it's because of lack of agent or what, that no one can kind of defend him. But I do know this, if Lamar Jackson can play, if he's healthy enough to play, he will play, and that's kind of all I can say for that."

One can perhaps safely guess Humphrey was referring to critics of Jackson who bemoan his absences from the lineup, including this year.

Jackson suffered a left ankle sprain on October 4 in the first half of his team's 23-17 win over the Tennessee Titans. He missed the remainder of that contest and the Ravens' next two games against the Atlanta Falcons (31-23 win) and Cleveland Browns (13-10 loss).

Jackson turned in limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday this week in advance of the team's home game against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Jackson has dealt with numerous injuries over the years and missed time, although he's still been in the lineup far more often than not since becoming the Ravens' QB1 in the middle of the 2018 season.

From 2019-2025, Jackson started 100 of a possible 117 games. He missed five games apiece in 2021 and 2022 but played every game in 2023 and 2024 minus the 2023 regular season opener, which occurred after Baltimore had already secured the AFC's No. 1 seed.

Jackson missed four games last year (three due to a hamstring injury, one due to a back contusion) and ultimately was slowed down by ailments overall .

Unfortunately, Jackson has now dealt with a new injury, but it appears he's at least trending in the right direction for a massive AFC North battle with the Bengals.

articles.title: New Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors as Colts RB Talks Potential Deal Before NFL Deadline
articles.summary: With the Indianapolis Colts off to a 2-4 start to the season, a handful of teams reportedly are eyeing star running back Jonathan Taylor.
articles.body:
With the Indianapolis Colts off to a 2-4 start to the season, a handful of teams reportedly are eyeing star running back Jonathan Taylor.

Per ESPN's Stephen Holder , several teams "would be open to a potential trade" for Taylor, but it is to be determined whether the Colts will look to be sellers at the deadline.

As his name begins to swirl in trade rumors, Taylor said his focus is on Indianapolis' upcoming matchup with the Minnesota Vikings.

NFL Insiders Name 'Sleeper' Trade Targets

"I haven't given any thought," he said when asked about his future. "That'd be crazy right now, especially because we've got a great Minnesota Vikings team that we have to go against. I think it would be a discredit and a disservice to my teammates and this whole organization to think about what could, what should, what may be."

The report follows the Colts' firing of general manager Chris Ballard earlier this week. Ballard drafted Taylor out of Wisconsin in 2020 and signed him to two contracts, including a two-year, $44 million extension in August.

Taylor has played up to the extension so far, recording the second-most carries (122) for the sixth-most rushing yards (492) and the second-most touchdowns (7).

But with the Colts struggling so far this season, and potential changes coming after Ballard's firing, it could be in the team's best interest to trade their star player and start building for the future.

The trade deadline is on Nov. 10, which doesn't give Indianapolis a lot of time to turn into a playoff contender. The Colts will face the undefeated Vikings this week before taking on the 4-2 Jacksonville Jaguars next week.

Along with Taylor, Holder noted that DeForest Buckner is another name that could be on the move before the deadline. The star defensive tackle has already picked up four sacks this season.

Buckner, who has been with the team since 2020, was clearly frustrated after the Colts' loss to the Tennessee Titans on Sunday.

"I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year," Buckner told reporters after the loss.

Perhaps moving on from Ballard will spark some new life in the Colts as they look to turn things around, but if things keep trending in the wrong direction, it could be the end of Taylor and more players' tenures in Indianapolis.

articles.title: Marshall Faulk Reveals Parkinson's Diagnosis, NFL Legend and Southern HC Says He's 'In a Good Place'
articles.summary: Pro Football Hall of Fame running back and Southern University football head coach Marshall Faulk revealed that he has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease.
articles.body:
Pro Football Hall of Fame running back and Southern University football head coach Marshall Faulk revealed that he has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease.

Faulk revealed the news on Dr. Sandeep Thakka's "Caring Neurologist" podcast.

The former Indianapolis Colts and St. Louis Rams superstar said he has been dealing with symptoms of the disease for a year-and-a-half. He first noticed an issue while he was playing golf.

"The rigidity in my hand, just sometimes after I play a lot or I practice a lot," Faulk said, per Toyloy Brown III of The Advocate . "I just thought it was, you know, normal nerves when putting and stuff like that."

During a biannual physical, Faulk's doctor advised him to get the situation checked out. A diagnosis followed, but thankfully, Faulk said he received his diagnosis in the early stages of the disease and considers himself "one of the lucky ones" for doing so.

Numerous ex-NFL players have revealed neurodegenerative disease diagnoses in recent years.

Of note, quarterback Brett Favre (in 2024) and running back Ahman Green (in 2026) told the public they were diagnosed with Parkinson's disease.

Running back Chris Johnson revealed last June that he has been diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (Lou Gehrig's disease).

The 53-year-old Faulk was one of his generation's greatest players. He was a versatile running back equally adept at rushing and receiving. Over his 12-year career (1994-2005), Faulk amassed 12,279 rushing yards and 6,875 receiving yards for 19,154 yards from scrimmage, ranking fifth all time in that category.

During the Rams' 1999 Super Bowl season, Faulk broke the 1,000-yard barrier in rushing (1,381 yards) and receiving (1,048 yards). He is one of three running backs to ever do so in a single season (Roger Craig, 1985; Christian McCaffrey, 2019).

Faulk was a first-ballot Hall of Famer, inducted as part of the class of 2011. He is also a member of the College Football Hall of Fame after his time at San Diego State (5,562 all-purpose yards, 62 career touchdowns, 1992 Heisman Trophy runner-up).

Faulk served as Colorado's running backs coach last year before becoming Southern's head coach this season. The 3-4 Jaguars have already eclipsed last year's two-win total.

Faulk recalled meeting Ali after his diagnosis and said he is now heartened by what he saw:

articles.title: The Lions’ heavy offense will stretch the Packers’ thin defensive line
articles.summary: Can Green Bay win another game with just four interior defensive linemen? Detroit will be a big test
articles.body:
You've heard this phrase a lot in the NFL over the last decade: Nickel is the new base. In some ways that's true, but it's really more like "nickel is the new base, when the opposing offense wants it to be."

Most NFL teams still match their defensive personnel to what opposing offenses throw out there, and the Green Bay Packers are no different. In general, defenses want to play as many cornerbacks and nickelbacks as the opposing offense has receivers.

So when offenses are in 11 personnel (three receivers, one back and one tight end) sets, defenses tend to play Nickel — which allows for a slot defender to "match" a slot receiver on the field. So far in 2026, the Packers have played 291 of their 292 snaps when they've faced 11 personnel offenses in Nickel (or Dime) sets — 99.7 percent.

When opposing offenses play heavier looks, be it multiple backs, multiple tight ends or even sets with extra offensive linemen or defensive linemen, NFL teams still match that with "base" personnel (a 3-4 in the Packers' case) an extra body in the box.

This year, Green Bay defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon's defense has played 75.9 percent of their snaps against these personnel packages (12/13/21/22) with a base 3-4 defense. No third receiver? That means no slot defender on the field. That's the basic math being done league-wide.

So is nickel the new base? Really only when the offense is playing 11 personnel. This, obviously, varies a lot team-by-team.

For example, last week the Packers faced the Dallas Cowboys, who have played 73 percent of their snaps in 11 personnel in 2026, the third-highest rate in the NFL . Against Green Bay, for whatever reason, they averaged 1.0 running backs per play and 1.1 tight ends per play — essentially living in 11 personnel full-time, even more so than their season-long averages.

From my perspective, I feel like the Packers caught a break. Green Bay, which almost always carries five interior defensive linemen on a 48-man gameday roster, was only able to carry four big bodies for the game because of Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Ford going on the injured reserve. Rookie Chris McClellan had to take over the starting 3-4 nose tackle spot in "base" looks for the first time, in place of Ford, and the only defensive lineman on the sideline when the starters were out there for limited 3-4 defense looks was Anthony Campbell, who had played all of nine career NFL snaps coming into the game. On top of that, Green Bay's Will linebacker position is a rotation between Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper right now, as starter Edgerrin Cooper is now on the injured reserve.

Campbell ended up playing 32 defensive snaps for the Packers in Week 6, even with the Cowboys playing mostly 11 personnel looks that mostly kept Green Bay to playing two defensive tackles at a time for most of the game. With how the Packers' lack of depth at the position played out on the defensive line, Dallas should have tried to wear out Green Bay's lack of numbers with multiple tight end looks (with slot defender Javon Bullard sidelined because of personnel matching) and tried to win that game in the second half against an exhausted front. Instead, Bullard played six of every seven snaps against the Cowboys.

The Packers dodged a bullet, but that doesn't mean that they're out of the woods. This week, they'll play a Detroit Lions team that likes to play a much heavier form of offense than Dallas. The Lions only play 11 personnel 58 percent of the time, a below-average rate in the NFL. They like to use multiple tight ends, or even linemen (both offensive or defensive) instead of that extra slot receiver.

They don't use multiple backs (average 1.0 backs played per play), but they play a second tight end (or extra lineman) close to every other play (1.5 tight ends per play).

It will be interesting to see if the Packers call up one of their two practice squad interior defensive linemen, David Blay Jr. or Mazi Smith, to add some depth to the game-day roster this week, but if Green Bay doesn't, they'll have to make it through with four linemen for a second straight game. This time, though, they won't be playing against a team that just wants to play with a full-time slot receiver, they'll be going against an offense that wants to play heavy offensive looks about every other play, the same looks that have forced an extra defensive lineman on the field for more than three-quarters of the Packers' defensive snaps in those situations throughout the season.

articles.title: Marshall Faulk discloses Parkinson's disease diagnosis
articles.summary: Hall of Fame running back and Southern University coach Marshall Faulk has disclosed that he has Parkinson's disease.
articles.body:
Hall of Fame running back and Southern University coach Marshall Faulk has disclosed that he has Parkinson's disease.

Via Jack Baer of Yahoo Sports, Faulk revealed the diagnosis in an appearance on the Caring Neurologist podcast.

"I get a physical twice a year," Faulk said. "I'm a little anal about my health. I literally asked my doctor because I noticed it as I was playing golf. I noticed the rigidity in my hand after I play a lot or practice a lot, I thought it was just normal nerves when putting and stuff like that. But it started to be times where I wasn't playing — I mean, where I was playing, but I wasn't in a match, and it would still do that.

"I was like, 'Wow, is that something? Is that normal?' And the doctor was like, ' You need to go get checked . You need to go have X, Y and Z done.'"

Faulk, a former NFL MVP, two-time NFL Offensive Player of the Year, three-time first-team All-Pro, and seven-time Pro Bowler, has been receiving treatment and taking medication.

"Since I've started on the medication, I don't really have a lot of issues," Faulk said. "I might sleep a little more. . . . Other than that, the rigidity in my hands, I still have that. Can't say that it's gotten worse. The little tremors that I get, they are what they are. I just pay attention to my gait, how I walk, when I'm working out, my ability to balance. It's still where it is.

"I don't look at it as something that's terminal. It's like, 'Hey, you get to live with this.' There's far worse things out there."

There's a known link between Parkinson's disease and football. It's one of the specific conditions that make a player who retired prior to the final settlement of the concussion class action automatically eligible for payment.

articles.title: Mark Sanchez’s change-of-plea hearing rescheduled to 2027, case reassigned to new judge
articles.summary: The long and winding legal road for Mark Sanchez, following an incident in Indianapolis that ended with him in the hospital, is going to continue for a bit l...
articles.body:
The long and winding legal road for Mark Sanchez, following an incident in Indianapolis that ended with him in the hospital, is going to continue for a bit longer.

After several court-date delays , Sanchez pleaded guilty last month , though it was unknown which charges he was pleading guilty to; among those he faced were battery causing serious injury, unauthorized entry of a motor vehicle, and public intoxication. A change-of-plea hearing in the criminal case was scheduled for Nov. 9 in Marion Superior Court.

However, this one too has been rescheduled.

According to Austin Hanson at Fox 59 , Sanchez's change-of-plea hearing has been moved. While changes in Indiana's public court reporting system on Wednesday initially suggested that the hearing had been canceled, further additions on Thursday confirmed the hearing had been rescheduled to Jan. 25, 2027.

Also noted in the Thursday update was that the judge assigned to the case, Helen W. Marchal, recused herself , though no reason was given for the recusal. The January hearing will take place before Judge Angela Dow Davis.

Sanchez, who was in Indianapolis to call a Colts game on Oct. 5 last year, was involved in a violent altercation outside his hotel with 69-year-old truck driver Perry Tole. The former NFL quarterback, who is believed to have been intoxicated , allegedly confronted the man inside the cab of his delivery truck. Tole, who claimed he believed his life was in danger, pepper-sprayed and stabbed Sanchez in self-defense. Both men were hospitalized after the incident. Fox Sports suspended Sanchez and later fired him .

Sanchez and former employer Fox also faced a civil suit stemming from the incident. According to court records, he and Tole reached an agreement in principle that will end the civil suit against the former NFL quarterback. Tole's attorneys are expected to file a motion to dismiss the civil case by Jan. 8.

articles.title: NFL Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk reveals Parkinson's diagnosis
articles.summary: The former Rams star discussed the diagnosis in a podcast episode.
articles.body:
Hall of Fame running back Marshall Faulk announced Thursday that he is battling Parkinson's disease.

Faulk, who won a Super Bowl and an MVP award as part of the "Greatest Show on Turf" Rams teams, made the announcement on "The Caring Neurologist" podcast with Dr. Sandeep Thakkar.

The 53-year-old isn't alone in fighting the disease, as Hall of Fame QB Brett Favre disclosed a Parkinson's diagnosis in 2024 and fellow running back Ahman Green also revealed a diagnosis earlier this year.

Here's what Faulk had to say about his condition.

Marshall Faulk reveals Parkinson's diagnosis

Faulk, who is the head football coach at FCS Southern University, revealed Thursday that he is battling Parkinson's disease, adding that he is still living a normal life in part because it was detected so early.

"Since I've started on the medication, I don't really have a lot of issues," Faulk said, explaining that he just has "little tremors" at the moment.

"I just pay attention to my gait, while I walk, when I'm working out, my ability to balance," Faulk said. "It's still where it is."

Faulk explained that he started to notice symptoms in his hand and was told by his doctor to get a closer evaluation when he brought it up during a physical.

"The rigidity in my hand, just sometimes after I play a lot or I practice a lot," Faulk said. "I just thought it was, you know, normal nerves when putting and stuff like that."

Faulk released a lengthier statement after appearing on the podcast:

Fortunately, Faulk said the early detection will give him a better quality of life going forward. Here's what you need to know about the disease.

Parkinson's disease is a progressive nervous system disorder that is not curable. While individuals with Parkinson's will have to live with it for the rest of their lives and face worsening symptoms as time progresses, the average lifespan of a person with the disease is not significantly reduced.

The most recognizable Parkinson's symptom is tremors in the arms and hands, according to the Mayo Clinic . Patients can also develop stiffness in the muscles that impacts their abilty to walk normally and raises the risk of falls.

Researchers from Boston University revealed in 2025 that they had found a connection between playing football and a higher risk of Parkinson's disease. Faulk joins Brett Favre, Ahman Green and Bernie Kosar as notable former players with the condition.

Amid Brown's quiet game, fans lamented another rough outing for the first-year Patriot.

Biggest takeaways from Bears' win over Patriots

The slow start from Brown comes after he had a career-high three drops last week against the Jets, recording just three receptions for 27 yards despite receiving 10 targets.

Brown said after the game that he was hoping to put the rough outing behind him and turn things around.

"Just tryna get going again, best foot forward, put this to be really fast," Brown said . "I'm gonna watch the tape. It's over. I'm gonna flush it."

The Patriots traded for Brown, hoping he could help them get back to the Super Bowl after coming up short against the Seattle Seahawks, but New England hasn't gotten much from him so far.

Clearly, he's still getting comfortable with his new team, and he'll look to find his rhythm so he can finally start contributing to the offense the way fans expected him to.

articles.title: Patriots close first half of Thursday Night Football with Rhamondre Stevenson TD thanks to bizarre misfire by Bears coverage
articles.summary: How did Rhamondre Stevenson score on this?
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears had a pretty good first half on Thursday night until there were three seconds left on the clock.

A last-gasp play by the New England Patriots resulted in a 48-yard receiving touchdown for running back Rhamondre Stevenson, whom the Bears left unchecked out of the backfield. Quarterback Drake Maye quickly found Stevenson, who had a blocker and dozens of yards of open field in front of him. It cut Chicago's lead to 20-14 at the time.

The Bears didn't end up paying for the mistake as they went on to win 30-24.

Even when Stevenson had the ball, the Bears' deep coverage should have been able to bring him down. However, a bad angle by cornerback Jaylon Johnson, a friendly fire collision between defensive backs Dillon Thieneman and Kyler Gordon, and a lack of speed from behind by cornerback Cam Lewis turned a four-on-two disadvantage into a winning play for New England.

This is not stuff you often see from an NFL defense.

The play doesn't get much better when viewed from a dots perspective.

Up to that point, the Bears had reason to feel good, with touchdowns by Luther Burden III and D'Andre Swift, plus a pair of Cairo Santos field goals, giving them a 20-7. Before that fateful play, they had outgained New England 217-179.

Momentum carries you only so far in the NFL, though.

articles.summary: Caleb Williams has no publicly confirmed girlfriend right now.
articles.body: Caleb Williams has no publicly confirmed girlfriend right now. The Chicago Bears quarterback is back on the field and healthy, and fans are once again asking who he is dating. Reports say he is single after a quiet split from Alina Thyregod, his Danish high school sweetheart, around August 2025. Online rumors later tied him to model Ash Kaashh after a Bears game, but that story fell apart. Williams rarely talks about his love life, so most of what is known comes from draft-night photos, social posts and a handful of early reports.Caleb Williams’ girlfriend and relationship timelineAlina Thyregod, a Danish woman reported to be building a career in fashion, is the most documented name in Caleb Williams’ dating history. The two met in Washington, D.C., as teenagers, and The Knot dates their first meeting to around 2018 or 2019. They reconnected in October 2023, in the middle of his last season at USC.Williams has confirmed part of that story himself. On The Pivot Podcast, he said he met his girlfriend in high school.Their public debut came at the 2024 NFL Draft in Detroit. Thyregod walked the red carpet with him, and she hugged him once the Bears made him the first overall pick. It was the first time most fans saw her.They marked one year together in October 2024, and Williams posted about it. Thyregod’s Instagram was private. Her TikTok clips, showing Williams making pottery, working on a puzzle and eating sushi, were the rare glimpses. His own feed stayed mostly about football. The public stretch of the relationship covered his whole rookie year, from draft night to the end of that season.Then things went quiet. Reports say the couple split around August 2025, just before his second season began. Details are thin, since neither has spoken about it publicly.Past relationships and rumors that did not hold upThe loudest rumor came in late 2025. Model and influencer Ashaley “Ash” Kaashh was linked to Williams after she attended a Bears game. The talk faded quickly. By January 2026, the New York Post reported she had gone public with Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs instead. One game-day appearance was all that rumor ever had behind it.Further back is Valerie Orana, a high school girlfriend from around 2020, a few years before the Thyregod chapter began.That relationship reportedly ended during his years at Oklahoma and USC, where he won the Heisman Trophy in 2022. articles.summary: A Thursday night quarterback duel went in the Chicago Bears' favor on Thursday evening as Caleb Williams led the home team to a 30-24 win over Drake Maye and the New England Patriots.
articles.body:
A Thursday night quarterback duel went in the Chicago Bears' favor on Thursday evening as Caleb Williams led the home team to a 30-24 win over Drake Maye and the New England Patriots.

The Chicago offense excelled on a night when the Bears honored late franchise legend Mike Ditka , who passed away on Oct. 9.

The three-point favorites (per FanDuel Sportsbook ) got notable fantasy performances from Williams, wide receiver Luther Burden III, tight end Colton Loveland and running back D'Andre Swift.

Biggest takeaways from Bears' win over Patriots

New England fought hard but was ultimately a step behind all night. Quarterback Drake Maye, running back Rhamondre Stevenson and tight ends Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon turned in good fantasy performances. It was an off-night for wideout A.J. Brown, though.

The Bears opened the scoring with Cairo Santos' 43-yard field goal in the first quarter. Chicago then followed with running back D'Andre Swift's four-yard touchdown rush. Bears wideout Luther Burden II set the play up with a 58-yard catch-and-run.

New England responded with a 74-yard drive capped by Drake Maye's seven-yard touchdown run by a nose.

Burden continued his dominant display, though, when he caught a quick pass on 3rd-and-17 and scored a 24-yard touchdown with 14 seconds left in the first half.

New England wasn't done, though. After the kickoff, Maye found Brown for 18 yards to get to the Bears' 48-yard line. May then hit Stevenson on a screen pass, and the running back did the rest, scampering for the end zone with no time remaining. Following the PAT, the Bears led 20-14 at half.

The Bears maintained the upper hand, though. They got the ball after halftime and marched down the field thanks largely to Loveland, who caught four passes for 47 yards and a score.

Loveland's touchdown was for 14 yards. He got through four Pats defenders along the way to the end zone.

New England fired right back, going 80 yards in nine plays capped by Maye's 30-yard TD pass to Raridon down the seam.

Chicago and New England went scoreless on the next four possessions, but the Bears then got the ball back on their own nine-yard line with 6:22 left.

It was the Williams show from there, and he had some help from wideout Rome Odunze. Williams hit Odunze for 21 yards on 3rd-and-9 from the Chicago 10-yard line, and he also found him for 21 more yards on 2nd-and-12 to get to midfield.

However, Williams took a sack from defensive tackle Christian Barmore that knocked the Bears back to the Pats' 40-yard line with 1:39 left.

Santos, who missed a 53-yard field goal on the Bears' last possession, then walked onto the field to try a career-long 58-yarder. He nailed it, giving the Bears a crucial two-possession edge.

Pats kicker Andres Borregales nailed a 47-yard field goal on New England's next drive with 37 seconds left. An onside kick followed, but Odunze recovered it. After one kneeldown, the Bears moved to 5-2. The Pats dropped to 4-3.

Both teams hit the road in Week 8. New England will play the Miami Dolphins in an AFC East showdown on Sunday, Nov. 1. Chicago will visit the Seattle Seahawks on Monday, Nov. 2.

Six weeks of play is more than enough to know how good a team is or isn't. Some may be swimming up stream, while others are handling business as expected.

Those squads who have failed to meet expectations can feel pressure as it increases with each passing week.

"Am I frustrated and p***ed off? You're damn right I am," Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters after his team's 2-4 start. "But I'm gonna roll my sleeves up and I'm gonna go to work. And I'm gonna solve it."

Proclamations mean nothing unless improvement is seen on the field.

Bleacher Report NFL analysts Brent Sobleski , Kris Knox , and Moe Moton will follow all of the action to break down which teams talked the talk and which ones actually walked the walk.

Bears 30, Patriots 24 Can Luther Burden III Continue as Chicago Bears No. 1 Target? The Chicago Bears traded DJ Moore this season after three straight seasons as the team's top wide receiver. The organization did so, because Rome Odunze was waiting in the wings after the Bears drafted the Washington product during the first round of the 2024 class. Odunze hasn't emerged as Chicago's WR1, though. Luther Burden is the more dynamic option, as seen Thursday against the New England Patriots. Burden was the Bears' leader with 31 receptions entering the team's latest contest. The second-year target exploded with four receptions for 130 yards and a score. In some ways, Burden has effectively replaced Moore, because they two receivers have similar skill sets. Like Moore, Burden is at his best after the catch, as evidenced by taking a simple smoke route and turning it into a 24-yard touchdown. His presence in the lineup could become more critical in the coming weeks. TE Cole Kmet Leaves Contest With Apparent Knee Injury Burden may be featured even more depending on the diagnosis of Cole Kmet's right knee. The veteran tight end's knee buckled during a fourth-quarter hit along the sidelines and needed to be carted off the field. Kmet provides the Bears with personnel flexibility. If he misses any time, Colston Loveland and Burden will be take on more responsibilities in the passing game. Meanwhile, third-round rookie Sam Roush can become a heavy in-line operator whenever head coach/offensive play-caller Ben Johnson opts to utilize 12 personnel.

Will the New England Patriots See AJ Brown Return to Form? The Patriots traded a first-round pick to acquire AJ Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles. The organization may already regret the deal. To be fair, Brown missed four came with an ankle injury. The 29-year-old target may need even more time getting back to game-speed. The Patriots' hope so, because Brown was a non-factor Thursday after not being on the same page with quarterback Drake Maye during Sunday's contest against the New York Jets.

In the end, the veteran target caught three passes for 48 yards. But he was added to create an impact for an offense that lacked a true WR1 last season. The Patriots will try and feed Brown the ball. He'll need to do something with those opportunities in the coming weeks or risk having the situation sour on him, much like it once did in Philadelphia. Patriots Can Alleviate Offensive Concerns with Greater Emphasis on Run Game Brown has yet to produce like a top target. New England is injured along the offensive line, with a pair of backup guards starting Thursday. A commitment to the run game can significantly help both matters. Granted, the Bears held a two-score lead during the second half on two different occasions. But the Patriots continued to chip away throughout the evening. In the end, New England's running backs carried the ball 13 times and averaged 3.4 yards per carry. This unit can't become so one-dimensional. The ability to run the ball will make life easier on the offensive line and create space for wide receivers.

Things got real this past week when the Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard after only six weeks. Granted, the move had been building for some time, but desperation is already setting in for some franchises.

Conversely, eight teams enter this weekend's play with four or more victories, including three remaining undefeated squads.

"I think he's really sharp mentally; he's accurate, he gets the ball out of his hands quickly," offensive coordinator Sean Mannion said of the Stanford graduate. articles.standfirst: Tras probar en el campus de New England Patriots, el defensa aspira a ser el primer español en la NFL que no fue formado en Estados Unidos
articles.summary: Tras probar en el campus de New England Patriots, el defensa aspira a ser el primer español en la NFL que no fue formado en Estados Unidos
articles.body: Cada vez más, el deporte arroja ejemplos de prometedores jóvenes que terminan brillando en una especialidad distinta, ayudados por la base forjada en los inicios. A Diego Paz (A Coruña 2003) le tiraban el atletismo y las vallas. Tenía nivel como para ser de los atletas que se entrenaban en el CAR de Madrid con Jesús Álvarez entre los que destacaba Sergio Fernández, el navarro que había batido el récord de España de 400 vallas en los Juegos Olímpicos de Río. Bajaba de 50 segundos sin obstáculos en la vuelta a la pista. Tenía 16 años. Pero a este tallo de 1,93 metros y 120 kilos de peso se le cruzaron las ganas de acompañar a un amigo suyo a una prueba con los Black Demonds y ahora está pendiente de que a finales de abril de 2027, New England Patriots, la franquicia que abanderó Tom Brady durante varios años y cuyo campus ya ha visitado, o cualquiera otra que se fije en él, lo reclute en el draft. Sería el cuarto español en alcanzar la gran liga en la historia tras Jess Rodríguez (1929) y los recientes Alejandro Villanueva y JJ Arcega. El primero sin desarrollar carrera previa en las inferiores en Estados Unidos. “Yo hasta 2022 no había visto un partido de fútbol americano. Ni sabía lo que era la NFL. Pero me atrapó”, cuenta. Fue el inicio de una ascensión continua. “De ahí pasé a los Barcelona Dragons, pero me cortaron porque no les convencí. Me fui a jugar a Finlandia [a los Seinäjoki Crocodiles y los Helsinki Wolverines]. Fui a ganar el campeonato y quedamos segundos. Regresé a España a los Madrid Bravos, donde aprendí mucho. Finalmente, me ficharon en Alemania (Rhein Fire) donde he liderado la estadística de sacks”. Casi como los portfolios que caen en Hollywood con los actores noveles, los futbolistas que quieren llamar la atención desde fuera de la liga universitaria estadounidense necesitan darse a conocer. En este vehículo que son las redes sociales, Paz comenzó a subir vídeos a las más convencionales y también a plataformas que visitan los ojeadores. Sabía de su dificultad, pero también que era posible. “Maceo Beard, un francés, lo consiguió con 26 años y yo pensé que, con 23, también tendría mis posibilidades”. De momento ha conseguido disfrutar de la oportunidad de los tentaderos de la NFL, el campus de los meritorios. Llegó con nervios, pero Diego se había preparado para eso. No para de aprender de aquí y de allá. Igual se ve cada podcast de Maxx Crosby, el defensive end de los Raiders, cada semana, que asimila otros conceptos del juego. “Me recogieron a las 7:30”, recuerda. “Las instalaciones son espectaculares. Nada más llegar nos tomaron las medidas, la envergadura y luego hicimos una prueba de explosividad y un reconocimiento médico. Me sorprendió la forma en la que está la gente que aspira. Allí habría 50 tíos que parecían un ejército de robots”. “¿Que lo pude hacer mejor?”, reflexiona. “Seguro, pero espero seguir aprendiendo de los errores y ya he visto lo que piden. A partir de aquí hay que trabajar. Y si hay que probar en otro club, lo haré. Como si termino jugando en otra liga o en Canadá. Pero estoy convencido de que jugaré en América”. La velocidad del atletismo, a pesar de que ha ganado un montón de kilos de musculatura -está en 120-, le permite correr las 40 yardas en 4,6 segundos. Un tiempo interesante. Como los que se le avecinan al joven que está poniendo todos los raíles para triunfar.

articles.title: NFL: Caleb Williams and Luther Burden propel Chicago Bears over Drake Maye's New England Patriots
articles.summary: Caleb Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns to lead the Chicago Bears to another impressive victory, defeating Drake Maye’s New England Patriots; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every minute of the playoffs and Super Bowl LXI
articles.body:
It was the second meeting between the young quarterbacks since they were part of the 2024 NFL draft. Maye, who was selected by New England at No 3, directed the Patriots to a 19-3 victory over Williams and the Bears when the longtime friends were rookies.

But Williams, the No 1 overall pick, leaned on Luther Burden and Colston Loveland while outlasting Maye and the Patriots in the rematch. Williams connected on 22 of 33 passes in his second game back after being sidelined by a hamstring injury.

The win moves the Bears to 5-2, keeping the pressure on NFC North leaders Minnesota, while the Patriots fall to 4-3.

Burden led Chicago with four catches for 130 yards, while Loveland added a 12-yard touchdown reception. Cairo Santos then struck a 58-yard field goal with 1:34 remaining, matching the franchise record and setting a new career best after missing a 53-yard attempt earlier in the fourth quarter.

Williams became the first Bears quarterback to throw for more than 300 yards in consecutive games since Mitch Trubisky managed the feat in three straight games in 2018.

Maye completed 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards and two touchdowns, while also rushing for a seven-yard score to get New England on the board with 11:33 remaining in the first half.

However, the Patriots quarterback was intercepted in the end zone by Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson late in the second quarter, with rookie tight end Eli Raridon the intended target.

After Santos' long field goal, Maye drove New England into range for Andy Borregales' 47-yarder with 37 seconds to go, before Chicago recovered the ensuing onside kick.

Rhamondre Stevenson had five catches for 93 yards and a touchdown for the Patriots. Raridon had a 30-yard TD catch in the third quarter.

It was Chicago's first home game since Bears legend Mike Ditka died on October 9. The team paid tribute to the Hall of Fame tight end and longtime coach with a pregame moment of silence, while fans among the 60,520 crowd at Soldier Field were handed fake moustaches in his honour.

Ditka's No 89 jersey was dotted throughout the stands, while fans also wore Bears sweaters in a nod to the sideline attire he sported as head coach.

Chicago opened a 20-7 lead on Burden's 24-yard touchdown with 14 seconds left in the first half. Burden got the ball on a screen on third-and-17, and Loveland, Kalif Raymond and Darnell Wright helped clear the way for his second TD reception of the season.

Set to receive the second-half kickoff, the Bears were in position to pull away. But the Patriots responded with Stevenson's 48-yard touchdown reception on the final play of the period.

Stevenson slipped out of the backfield and Maye lobbed the ball over the head of Bears safety Cam Lewis. Stevenson ran away from Lewis and got a downfield block from DeMario Douglas before cutting past Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson on his way to the end zone.

Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams:

"You play against another good team on a primetime game in a short week, these games are awesome because you get to see who you are as a team.

"That's who we are. We're a smashmouth football team, an innovative team. And when things happen and things don't go our way and the water is rocky, we stay steady."

articles.title: 'They're young superstars': Caleb Williams, Drake Maye deliver fireworks but Bears QB does just enough to top Patriots
articles.summary: The off-script playmaking of Williams and Maye makes them two of the top offensive creators in the sport. It was the premier attraction.
articles.body:
CHICAGO — On the surface, quarterbacks Caleb Williams and Drake Maye appear quite different. Williams unapologetically wears his emotions on his sleeve for the Chicago Bears and dons his fashion-forward fits everywhere . Meanwhile, a soft-spoken Maye still has a bit of a Southern drawl, and his "aw, shucks" demeanor in front of a mic belies his intensity on the gridiron for the New England Patriots.

The 6-foot-1 Williams is 3 inches shorter than Maye. Williams' escapability wowed in the pre-draft process. Maye's prototypical size and traits made him a sparkly prospect.

But they were separated by only two picks in the 2024 NFL Draft, there's an even smaller gap between their somewhat parallel pro careers, and, as Bears backup signal-caller Tyson Bagent told Yahoo Sports postgame, "they're more similar than not."

" Same draft class, top-three picks," said Williams' center, Garrett Bradbury, who snapped the ball to Maye all last season during the Patriots' run to the Super Bowl, "and they're young superstars. They really are."

The off-script playmaking of Williams and Maye makes them two of the top offensive creators in the sport. It was the premier attraction during this week's iteration of Thursday Night Football, a game in which Williams' Bears and Maye's Patriots at one point combined for seven scoring drives in an eight-possession span.

The lone exception was a Patriots series that ended with a Maye interception in the end zone. On a night when both he and Williams piled up more than 300 passing yards while stoically navigating an abundance of pressure, that turnover was a distinguishing factor in Williams outdueling his longtime counterpart in Chicago's 30-24 victory .

"Great quarterback. He's been a great quarterback for years," Williams said at the podium, when asked about trading blows with Maye. "When that happens, you want to go out there, and [be like], 'Let's go get one. Let's put the score back up. Let's match that from there.' I think we did just that."

To effectively seal the game, though, the Bears needed insurance, not an equalizer. A fourth-quarter drive that began with Williams zipping an eye-catching throw and wide receiver Rome Odunze making a jaw-dropping grab on third-and-9 concluded with Cairo Santos drilling a career-long 58-yard kick , which is tied for the third-longest field goal in Soldier Field history.

Santos' clutch kick gave the Bears a nine-point advantage with 1:34 to go. New England tacked on three points afterward but couldn't recover a last-ditch onside kick.

Odunze rebounded from committing offensive pass interference in the second quarter on a pass he couldn't haul in that could have resulted in a touchdown, and Santos bounced back from plunking the right upright on a 53-yard attempt earlier in the fourth that would have also put the Bears up two scores.

Overcoming adversity was the name of the game for a Bears team that seamlessly turned the page after allowing a dump-off pass to Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson transform into a 48-yard touchdown on the final play of the first half .

"You find out what you're made of," head coach Ben Johnson said postgame. "And I know we got the right guys in this locker room, that they can handle anything that's thrown their way. They have a lot of belief in each other, too. I think that's a really big part of it — they know that even when things get a little bit funky or haywire, that we can right the ship and get it going back the right direction real quick."

Williams, Maye finding their groove after experiencing early-season hardship

Just as Wlliams and Maye broke out in the 2025 season, they each broke down early in the 2026 season. Williams suffered a hamstring injury late in Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . His emotional reaction to the setback was memed profusely once reports suggested the issue was much less severe than expected; however, after missing three games, a ticked off Williams admonished the "false" reports he felt misconstrued what he ultimately described as a "pretty serious" hamstring "tear."

Even before Williams went down, Maye was dealing with turmoil. With a chance to avenge the Super Bowl defeat in the league's first game of the 2026 season, he threw a trio of interceptions against the Seattle Seahawks, worst among them a vexing last-second pick in the end zone. Maye threw three more INTs and no touchdowns over the next two outings. It seemed as though the sky was falling in New England before it could settle into its winter gray.

Since returning to the field, Williams has recorded back-to-back 300-yard passing games ( he's the first Bears QB to do that since Mitchell Trubisky in 2018 ). Meanwhile, over the past four outings, Maye has posted a 12:2 touchdown-to-interception ratio that's much more like the numbers he was registering as the runner-up for the NFL MVP award last season.

"That position is so important in this league," Bradbury told Yahoo Sports in the locker room. "And to have that position in that stage of their career playing the way both of them are playing, you got to feel good about your franchise going the right direction."

Last season, New England won its first AFC title since the 2018 campaign, and Chicago won its first playoff game since the 2010 season. Winners of four of their last five games, the Bears are now 5-2. While Thursday's defeat drops the Patriots to 4-3, it's noticeable that Maye has "kind of caught his rhythm," according to Johnson.

"Just watching Drake Maye play, I mean, he's an outstanding player," Johnson said. "It's very hard to bottle him up. You only rush four, and he finds a way. If he doesn't see anything down the field, he'll find an open gap and skirt on through.

"I think what's really impressive is how he can find these little outlets and these dumps, where they're still running vertical for catch-and-run opportunities."

Maye, who finished with 321 yards, 2 touchdowns and 1 interception on 24-of-31 passing, adjusted to a Bears defense that came out firing on all cylinders after heating up the Atlanta Falcons in Week 6, a week when Chicago led all teams with what Next Gen Stats charted as a 46.2% pressure rate. From the jump, Dennis Allen's unit attacked a Patriots offensive line that was starting reserve guards. Chicago frequently walked up several defenders to the line of scrimmage and either blitzed or broke out into a simulated pressure. Early on, that havoc seemed to befuddle the Patriots.

Eventually, New England adapted. Keeping a running back and/or tight end in to assist with protection helped. So did Maye's legs, which he notably used on the Patriots' first touchdown, ultimately scoring while reaching the ball past the goal line before he was down.

Although Maye clocked out with only four carries and 26 rushing yards, those figures don't do his mobility justice.

"It's like you think you have everything covered," Bears rookie safety Dillon Thieneman told Yahoo Sports afterward, "and then if you don't have a good enough rush or contain the pocket, then he's able to get out and make it a big play."

On New England's first drive of the second half, Maye broke free from the grasp of Thieneman on a third-and-7, continued to move to his right and then located tight end Hunter Henry for a 13-yard pickup.

That drive culminated with Maye lofting a perfectly placed toss to another tight end, rookie Eli Raridon, dismissing the Bears' blitz with a 30-yard TD strike that made it a 27-21 game.

There were several plays Maye conducted like those. And yet, even so, Williams might have authored more big-time throws. After making his layups while hitting on 30-of-36 passes against the Falcons last time out — a performance that, at the time, placed him first among all qualifying passers in completion percentage — Williams consistently pulled the ripcord Thursday amid his 308-yard, two-touchdown spectacle.

"Be decisive. Let it rip," Williams said postgame. "That's always something I preach to myself each week before every game: Decisiveness wins."

Williams didn't flinch, not after tight end Colston Loveland dropped catchable balls and not after Odunze's missed touchdown opportunity in the first half.

Immediately following Odunze's OPI penalty, Williams told his wideout that he'd be coming back to him.

"We didn't know when. And it ended up being a big part of the game."

On that aforementioned third-and-9, the Bears were leading by six points and needed to at least kill clock with about five minutes to go and the ball at their own 10-yard line.

Williams launched a missile. It flew just over the fingertips of leaping Patriots safety Kevin Byard III and into the hands of an outstretched Odunze for a 21-yard gain.

"He's on the money more often than not," said Odunze, who collected another 21 yards two snaps later on that FG drive. "We got to be in the right positions to make those plays, and we know he's going to get the ball to us."

Loveland, after winding up with a team-high seven catches, 69 receiving yards and a touchdown, added: "[Caleb's] got that swag on him right now."

articles.title: Why Jets must not sell farm for 2027 NFL Draft amid another disappointing season
articles.summary: The New York Jets are headed towards familiar territory yet again. After six weeks of action, the Jets are at 2-4 to start the year. While they’ve had some e...
articles.body:
The New York Jets are headed towards familiar territory yet again. After six weeks of action, the Jets are at 2-4 to start the year. While they've had some encouraging performances as of late, the team is still headed towards another year of missing the postseason. With the trade deadline approaching, though, they find themselves at a crossroads yet again.

Should the Jets hold another fire sale at the trade deadline?

It's a valid question to ask. New York has virtually no hope of making it to the postseason, barring an extreme glow-up by the entire team and the Bills and Patriots collapsing inexplicably. For most teams, the most sound decision would be to sell the farm and try to reload for the upcoming season with exciting rookies and whatnot.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

However, the Jets are not most teams. While New York could try to acquire more draft assets this year, they don't need to sell the entire team to kickstart their rebuild… because they already have the draft capital that most teams desire.

Jets need not sell the farm for the 2027 NFL Draft

There's one simple reason why the Jets don't need to hold a fire sale at the trade deadline this year: they've already done something like that last year. If you'll recall, New York was involved in two of the biggest midseason trades in 2025. They traded cornerback Sauce Gardner to the Indianapolis Colts and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams to the Dallas Cowboys for a haul of first-round picks. They netted two first-round picks from the Colts and one tackle from the Cowboys, giving them a boatload of draft picks for the future.

Looking at the Jets' draft haul for 2027, they already have a lot of picks for the upcoming draft. Most importantly, they have three first-round draft picks in 2027, along with their own draft picks for next year. In total, New York has nine draft picks for 2027 (three firsts, one pick from Rounds 2 to 5, and two sixth-rounders). The high number of first-round picks is notable, as teams often just have one or two firsts in every draft.

The position of the first-rounders is also worth noting. The Colts are struggling this season, and it wouldn't be a surprise to see that first-rounder become a top-10 pick or better. The Cowboys are slightly better than the Colts, but they're also likely to finish outside the postseason race. That, combined with the Jets' own 2027 first, means that New York might have three picks inside the top-11 next year.

Trading your valuable players for more draft picks is a valid strategy, yes. However, a team also needs to be careful about trading too many pieces in the name of drafting more young players. After all, you still need to have players on your team to build around. The Jets don't have many intriguing pieces to trade that aren't integral pieces to their future plans.

Former first-round pick Will McDonald IV is a good trade candidate, but beyond him, the options are either too valuable or wouldn't net enough value. The Jets wouldn't trade Garrett Wilson or Breece Hall, no matter how many firsts a team might offer. AD Mitchell and Geno Smith aren't needle-movers for other teams. New York is much better off just evaluating their talents this season and waiting for a good offer from a different team in the league.

There's also one looming possibility for the Jets, and that's to leverage their draft picks to trade for a player themselves. Still, the best play for the Jets at the trade deadline is to simply just stay put, wait if any offer entices them, and just ride the wave.

articles.title: ‘Dear God,’ ‘Super-Team Curse Is So Real’ — NFL World Takes Notice as Another Injury Concern Emerges For Rams Star Puka Nacua
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams’ season is turning into a growing injury nightmare, and Puka Nacua could be the latest star to miss some time. The wide receiver left Th...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams' season is turning into a growing injury nightmare, and Puka Nacua could be the latest star to miss some time. The wide receiver left Thursday's practice early with a calf injury, putting his availability for Sunday's Week 7 clash against the Las Vegas Raiders in doubt.

Los Angeles entered the 2026 season with Super Bowl hopes, but a growing list of injuries has made that goal harder to reach. Their recent 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals dropped them to 2-4 and the bottom of the NFC West. Now, Nacua's injury has given fans and analysts another reason to worry as the team looks to get its season back on track.

Nacua's injury has added to the frustration surrounding a Rams team already missing several key players. Wide receiver Davante Adams is on Injured Reserve with a severe hamstring injury, while tight end Terrance Ferguson remains sidelined with an ankle issue.

The defense has also taken hits, with Myles Garrett recovering from knee surgery, Poona Ford out for the season with a triceps injury, and Kobie Turner expected to miss four to six weeks with a groin strain.

Linebacker Nate Landman remains in concussion protocol, while cornerback Trent McDuffie has also dealt with a groin injury. Kicker Blake Grupe is out for the season after tearing his ACL.

The growing injury list has prompted strong reactions from fans and analysts. ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky summed up his reaction in two words, writing, "Dear God."

The Sleeper News channel also expressed frustration, posting , "Not Puka man."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Analyst Field Yates shared a similar reaction, writing, "Ah crap."

One fan pointed to the number of injuries affecting the team, saying, "'Super Team' curse so real in the NFL."

Analyst Holden Cantor also appeared frustrated, writing, "I'm out man."

Meanwhile, analyst Derek Brown questioned the Rams' offseason draft decisions in light of their current problems. "I feel like MAYBE the Rams should have drafted a WR this year instead of a QB & a TE," Brown wrote.
